column3: NKJV names “God” and “Abraham” for clarity, where the Greek has “He” and “him.”
NKJV has “all the land of Egypt,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “all Egypt.”
NKJV has “grain in Egypt,” following the Textus Receptus wording.
NKJV has “Hamor, the father of Shechem,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Hamor in Shechem.”
NKJV has “had sworn,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “had granted.”
NKJV lacks “over Egypt,” as does the Textus Receptus; the critical text includes it.
NKJV has “an Angel of the Lord,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “an angel.”
